readerQuestion: How can I prepare for a difficult work conversation when I do not feel confident yet?
readerPayoff: The reader can choose one bounded uncomfortable conversation, prepare a truthful first line and rehearse one realistic objection without pretending the rehearsal predicts the person.
headline: Rehearse the uncomfortable conversation before confidence arrives
opening: Waiting until you feel confident can keep a necessary conversation on your calendar for weeks. Choose one bounded conversation, write the outcome you need and prepare the first sentence you can honestly say.
newcomerBackground: Dorie Clark's practitioner advice distinguishes confidence from a willingness to choose some uncomfortable career moves deliberately. A voice-capable AI can provide practice turns, but it cannot know the real person or workplace.
causalOutline: Waiting for confidence can postpone a necessary conversation.
A clear purpose and truthful first sentence make the conversation easier to begin.
One bounded rehearsal exposes wording the user wants to improve.
The real conversation still requires human judgment about the person, power and consequences.

evidenceBoundary.establishes: Dorie Clark recommends deliberately choosing some uncomfortable career moves, including difficult conversations, and ChatGPT Voice currently supports spoken back-and-forth practice.
evidenceBoundary.doesNotEstablish: It does not establish that discomfort guarantees advancement, that AI predicts a person's reaction, or that AI makes a dangerous, discriminatory or legally sensitive situation safe.

mechanismBridge.objectLocationSentence: The rehearsal contains the user's first line, one likely objection and her spoken response.
mechanismBridge.attackDefinitionSentence: The practical failure is waiting to feel confident without preparing the first exchange.
mechanismBridge.evidenceRecoverySentence: The user writes down the sentence she wishes she had said and still decides how to approach the real person.

actionOpening: Choose one bounded conversation and write the first honest sentence.
incidentAction: If the situation involves danger, discrimination, legal rights or serious consequences, stop the AI rehearsal and seek appropriate human help.
evidenceParagraphBreaksAfter: This is practice for clarity, not a prediction of how the real person will respond.

centralInstruction.opening: Do not wait for confidence before preparing.
centralInstruction.action: Write the purpose and first line, then rehearse one likely objection.
centralInstruction.closing: What sentence do you want ready when the real conversation begins?
prohibitedRestatements: AI will tell you what they will say

evidenceSequence: Dorie Clark describes difficult conversations as one kind of discomfort people may choose deliberately before they feel fully ready.
OpenAI's current Voice documentation supports spoken back-and-forth and warns that ChatGPT can make mistakes.
LAiDIES limits the tool's role to low-stakes rehearsal and leaves the real decision with the user.

readerSources.label: Dorie Clark — Why Successful People Choose Discomfort Over Safety

voicePlan.move: Confidence is not the entry ticket; preparation is.
voicePlan.teachingJob: Separate the feeling of confidence from the small preparation the reader can control.
voicePlan.limit: Preparation does not remove power differences, danger or consequences.
voicePlan.readerFacingLimit: AI can create practice turns; it cannot predict the person or decide whether the situation is safe.
voicePlan.humanTruth: A hard conversation can sit on the calendar while someone waits for a feeling that may arrive only after acting.
voicePlan.mechanismMappingSentence: The rehearsal makes the first exchange concrete enough to practise without pretending it is the real conversation.

warmthLines.line: Confidence is not the entry ticket; preparation is.
The AI is a rehearsal partner, not the office oracle.

sectionPlan.heading: Prepare the first exchange
sectionPlan.readerJob: Give useful non-AI career guidance, a clear purpose and exact first-line example before introducing AI.

sectionPlan.heading: Use one low-stakes rehearsal
sectionPlan.readerJob: Connect the advice to one bounded voice-AI practice method and explain why it helps.

sectionPlan.heading: Know where practice stops
sectionPlan.readerJob: State the human, privacy and high-stakes boundaries and give the one try-today move.

work.example: A conversation about a moved deadline begins with a purpose, one honest question and one rehearsed objection.

nonWork.reason: This exact Career / Work-Life item is deliberately workplace-facing; a home rehearsal would belong in a different lane.

usefulLanding: Choose one bounded conversation, write the first line and rehearse one round.
routingReason: The career advice stands on its own before an earned AI connection; it is not Paige workflow advice, Promptoscope or a news report.
